claim: Trace argument string values retain up to 1,024 characters plus a `…(truncated)` marker; a per-step argument tree over 16 KiB compact ASCII-escaped JSON, 1,024 nodes including keys, or eight nesting levels below its root is replaced by `{}`; invalid JSON-shaped values are dropped; both truncation and dropping set `arguments_truncated: true`; the whole-trace size cap remains.
source_excerpt: Trace argument string values retain up to 1,024 characters plus `…(truncated)`. A per-step argument tree exceeding 16 KiB of compact ASCII-escaped JSON, 1,024 nodes (including keys), or eight nesting levels below its root is replaced by `{}`. Invalid JSON-shaped values are also dropped. Both truncation and dropping set `arguments_truncated: true`; the existing whole-trace size cap remains. Short values are preserved, including any sensitive content they contain: this is a size bound, not secret redaction. Enable details only for trusted debugging clients.

claim: `_request_metadata(ctx)` returns `{}` on extraction failures or invalid/oversized metadata; extras are limited to 64 top-level keys, 16 KiB of compact ASCII-escaped JSON, 1,024 nodes including keys, and eight nesting levels below the root; traversal stops at the limits and oversized trees are never partially forwarded.
source_excerpt: - **Fail-secure on metadata extraction.** `_request_metadata(ctx)` in [src/sqllens/server.py](../../../src/sqllens/server.py) returns `{}` on extraction failures or invalid/oversized metadata. Extras are limited to 64 top-level keys, 16 KiB of compact ASCII-escaped JSON, 1,024 nodes including keys, and eight nesting levels below the root. Traversal stops at the limits; oversized trees are never partially forwarded. Dynamic rules then block on missing values. This bounds propagation after MCP parsing, not HTTP request parsing.
